hero.label: Prague → Graz
hero.intro: 450 km south through Bohemia and Austria to the City of Design. Schlossberg, the Kunsthaus, and the Styrian mountains behind — four and a half to five hours, one fixed price.
hero.imageAlt: Graz — private chauffeur transfer from Prague to Graz

openingParagraphs: A private transfer from Prague to Graz covers approximately 450 km and takes about 4.5 to 5 hours door to door. Fixed fare starts at €{ePrice} in a Mercedes E-Class for up to 3 passengers; groups of up to 6 travel in the V-Class from €{vPrice}; the S-Class is available from €{sPrice} for executive or VIP travel. Every booking includes the driver's time, fuel, Czech and Austrian motorway vignettes, the A9 Pyhrn tunnel tolls, bottled water, onboard Wi-Fi, phone charger, and child seats on request at no extra cost. Nothing is added at drop-off. The fare is agreed before departure and does not change regardless of traffic or waiting time at your destination. Stops en route — České Budějovice or Linz — are available at the fixed fare when arranged at booking. Your chauffeur monitors traffic before every departure and reroutes without asking if there is a delay.
This is not a shared shuttle. A private Mercedes, one chauffeur, and a fare that does not change.

paragraphs: From a Prague pickup in Old Town, Vinohrady, Malá Strana, or the airport, your chauffeur takes the D3 motorway south through Tábor to České Budějovice and on to the Austrian border. On the Austrian side the S10 Mühlviertel expressway carries you down to Linz on the Danube. From Linz the A9 Pyhrn motorway runs south through Upper Austria and Styria — through the Bosruck and Gleinalm tunnels and past the limestone ranges of the Northern Alps — and into Graz. A detour via Vienna is possible on request, but it is not the main road.

The Czech–Austrian border at Dolní Dvořiště–Wullowitz is inside Schengen — invisible, no stops, no document checks. You arrive at the UNESCO Old Town, one of the best-preserved historic centres in Central Europe, with the Schloßberg and the Uhrturm rising above the Mur and the Kunsthaus — the friendly alien — glowing blue across the river.

Your chauffeur watches Friday-afternoon outbound traffic from Prague and the weather on the Pyhrn motorway before every departure. If there is a closure, they reroute without asking. You are not paying for traffic; you are paying for time.

includedIntro: The fixed price covers everything from Prague pickup to Graz drop-off. The car, the chauffeur, the fuel, the tolls, both vignettes. Business visit, design conference, or a Styrian weekend — your driver handles the route while you focus on the destination.
inclusions: A black Mercedes — E-Class, S-Class, or V-Class depending on group size and preference. Every vehicle under three years old.
A professional chauffeur — fluent English and Czech. German on request.
Fuel, all tolls, the Czech vignette, and the Austrian motorway vignette. Nothing is charged on top.
Door-to-door service — pickup and drop-off at the exact address you specify, not a parking lot.
Bottled water, phone charger, and WiFi in the rear cabin.
Waiting time at pickup — 15 minutes free at any address.
Child seats on request — rear-facing infant, forward-facing toddler, or booster. No additional charge.
Same-day return — 10% off the return leg if booked together, or add hourly city rental.
fleetNote: All vehicles are late-model Mercedes-Benz, maintained to manufacturer standard. Child seats available on request at no charge.

journeyStops.note: Pickup from your hotel, office, or Prague Airport (PRG). Driver waits up to 60 minutes at the airport.
Upper Austria's capital on the Danube sits naturally en route and is available as a lunch stop or a short visit before the A9 south.
A stop at a viewpoint, a village, or a Styrian wine tavern off the A9. Your route, your pace.
Drop-off at any Graz address, Graz Airport (GRZ), or the Schloßberg below the Uhrturm.

goodToKnow.label: Border crossing
goodToKnow.value: Czech–Austrian at Dolní Dvořiště–Wullowitz — Schengen, no passport checks for EU citizens.

goodToKnow.label: Tolls
goodToKnow.value: Czech vignette, Austrian vignette, and the A9 Pyhrn tunnel section tolls all included in the quoted price.

goodToKnow.label: Return transfer
goodToKnow.value: Book both directions together for a reduced rate. Most clients overnight in Graz.

goodToKnow.label: Onward routing
goodToKnow.value: Vienna is 190 km north, the Slovenian border 60 km south. Prestigo can extend your transfer as a single booking.

chauffeurNarrative: Your chauffeur will meet you at Václav Havel Airport or in front of your central Prague address — not a parking lot across the street, not a meeting point a ten-minute walk away. At the airport, they are inside the arrivals hall with a Prestigo tablet displaying your name, and the black Mercedes is already parked at the door.

Conversation is a choice. If you want a quiet cabin for four and a half hours of work or rest, the chauffeur will read that signal and let you be. If you want context on Graz — the Habsburg imperial seat era when it was one of the capitals of Inner Austria, the UNESCO listing of the Old Town in 1999, the UNESCO City of Design title earned in 2011, or the Styrian traditions of crisp white wine and dark pumpkin seed oil from the hills south of the city — your chauffeur knows it.

Phone charger, bottled water, and WiFi are already in the cabin. Temperature is set to your preference. A real rest stop is planned halfway — usually a proper rest area on the D3 near Tábor or a Raststätte on the Austrian A9 before Graz — not a petrol pump beside the motorway.

items.title: Fixed fare, no surprises
items.body: The price you see is the price you pay. Fuel, Czech vignette, Austrian vignette, Pyhrn tunnel tolls, driver time. Nothing added at drop-off on Herrengasse.

items.title: Owned fleet, vetted chauffeurs
items.body: Prestigo operates its own Mercedes fleet. Every vehicle under three years old. Every chauffeur background-checked, bilingual, trained for long international routes.

items.title: The route, your way
items.body: If you want to break the drive in Linz, or detour via Vienna, that is included. For Styrian wine country detours south of the city, the chauffeur knows the route.

faqs.q: How long does a private transfer from Prague to Graz take?
faqs.a: Approximately 4.5 to 5 hours door-to-door. The route runs south on the D3 through Tábor and České Budějovice, crosses into Austria at Dolní Dvořiště–Wullowitz, follows the S10 to Linz, then the A9 Pyhrn motorway south through Upper Austria and Styria into Graz. Traffic around Prague during Friday afternoon rush hour can add 20 to 30 minutes.

faqs.q: How much does a chauffeur from Prague to Graz cost?
faqs.a: Fixed fare from €{ePrice} in Mercedes E-Class (up to 3 passengers), €{vPrice} in V-Class (up to 6 passengers), or €{sPrice} in S-Class. Prices include fuel, the Czech motorway vignette, the Austrian motorway vignette, the A9 Pyhrn tunnel tolls, and driver time. No hidden charges.

faqs.q: Can I book a same-day round trip to Graz?
faqs.a: It is workable but heavy. A round trip is close to ten hours on the road before any time on site, so most clients choose to overnight in Graz and return the next morning. If you need the chauffeur to move around the city with you, add hourly city rental.

faqs.q: Are there border crossings on the way?
faqs.a: Yes, one. The Czech–Austrian border at Dolní Dvořiště–Wullowitz is inside the Schengen Area — no passport checks, no stops. Non-EU passengers should carry valid travel documents as a precaution.

Yes. Rear-facing infant seats, forward-facing toddler seats, and booster seats are available at no extra cost. Please specify your child's age at booking so the correct seat is installed before pickup.
A German-speaking chauffeur is available on request, which many clients appreciate for a Graz run. Every Prestigo chauffeur speaks fluent English and Czech as standard.

relatedRoutesIntro: Graz sits at the end of the long southern run through Linz and the Austrian Alps. Many clients combine the Graz transfer with a stop in Linz on the way, or with Vienna, Bratislava, or Budapest as separate legs. Every Prestigo route has the same fixed-fare model, the same fleet, and the same chauffeurs.
